#2668. Week 11 NFL Power Rankings: Each Team’s Second-Half Outlook

Although it might be hard to believe, we've not only crossed the halfway point of the 2026 NFL regular season, but the trade deadline has come and gone, too. While the NFC playoff picture is muddied with nine very good teams fighting for seven playoff spots, the AFC is a little easier to decipher. With the stretch run upon us, it's time to take a deeper dive into every team's second-half outlook. While many are still competing for a playoff spot, others will need to find meaning amid lost seasons. We'll dive into all of that and more in our Week 11 installment of WCG NFL Power Rankings.

Second-Half Outlook: Get healthy and continue their push for the No. 1 seed in the NFC

The first nine games of the season have been nothing short of impressive for the 49ers. Looking back to the preseason, nobody had the 49ers running away with a loaded NFC West, especially with the defending Super Bowl Champions and the overwhelming 2026 Super Bowl favorites. Instead, Kyle Shanahan has taken one of the league's oldest rosters and survived multiple impact injuries. We'll see if they can keep the pace up over the back half of the year, but this is one of the more well-rounded rosters in the league this season.

Second-Half Outlook: Hope that the defense can round into form and support one of the league's elite offenses

The addition of Amani Hooker should be a big one for this Buffalo defense, but it's fair to wonder if one player will be enough to turn the tide for a struggling defense. Some might point to their Week 8 and 9 performances as hope, and while that might be the case, the opponents need to be noted. The good news is that this is an experienced roster with an MVP-caliber quarterback. We'll see if they finally have enough to get them over the hump in the AFC. Like last year, it's wide open and theirs for the taking.

Second-Half Outlook: Ride a favorable schedule and find a way to earn the No. 1 seed down the stretch

The Bills might have better odds to win the Super Bowl, but the Jaguars have a strong argument for being the more well-rounded team. Simply put, Jacksonville has been dominant for the majority of the season, and the additions of Jordan Davis and Devin Godchaux should help stabilize the middle of their defense. If quarterback Trevor Lawrence can continue his ascension, this is going to be the toughest out for anybody in the AFC.

Second-Half Outlook: Survive a brutal schedule down the stretch and hope that Jeffery Simmons continues to be a difference-maker

Once dubbed a prime regression candidate heading into the regular season, the Bears have survived without Caleb Williams for three games and somehow continue to play much better defense than the numbers suggest. Williams' Year 3 jump has been notable, even with a four-interception game in Week 9. The talent on offense is evident, and their ceiling feels safe with Ben Johnson calling plays. How far they go this season will come down to the defense, especially the secondary. We'll see if not making another move at the deadline comes back to bite them.

Second-Half Outlook: Continue to build continuity on defense and hope that they'll be good enough to get them over the hump down the stretch and into January

When quarterback Joe Burrow is healthy, this offense is hard to stop. Their running game has been spotty at best, but with Ja'Marr Chase and Tee Higgins on the field, it really hasn't mattered. Their defense is much improved from previous seasons, but there are still some holes that could expose them against better teams. The AFC North appears to be coming down to the Bengals and Steelers, and at full strength, I'd take Cincinnati without much thought. Similar to the Bills, their defense will dictate how far they can go this season. So far, so good.

Second-Half Outlook: Hope that Patrick Mahomes is healthy enough to enjoy his new offensive weapon and push the Broncos for the AFC West title

Despite their 5-0 start to the season, I'm still not ready to say the Chiefs are all the way "back". They've continued to ignore the wide receiver position, and while the addition of Josh Downs is a step in the right direction, there's still a lot to be desired on the offensive side of the ball when it comes to personnel. Keeping Mahomes healthy will be key, and their Week 9 scare could have been season-altering. They aren't out of the race in the AFC West, but the offensive production is going to need to jump in the second half for them to win the division.

Second-Half Outlook: Rely on a weak schedule down the stretch and hope that the defense can continue to play at the same level

In many ways, the start of this season has been eerily similar to how they looked last season. So far, the biggest difference is that they are winning those close games that they couldn't pull off last season. The offense has looked great under Drew Petzing, but their season will come down to how much their defense can sustain over the final eight games. Following a rough start, they've been playing much better as of late, but there are still plenty of questions on that side of the ball. In a loaded NFC North, they must take advantage of their favorable schedule. Missing Jack Campbell and Aidan Hutchinson will hurt, especially over time.

Second-Half Outlook: Hope that the presence of Kirk Cousins is enough to support an elite defense

Defensively, there isn't a better unit in the league. Frankly, with as poor as their offense has played to this point, Brian Flores' group is the only thing separating them from a losing record. With that in mind, the addition of Cousins comes at a great time. Not only are they in the midst of their toughest stretch of the season, but the veteran quarterback knows the offense and should be able to hit the ground running. Even if he's still the fourth-best quarterback in his own division, the ceiling for the offense is considerably higher than it was just a week ago. We saw that on Sunday in Green Bay. Now, we'll see if that's good enough to separate themselves in a loaded NFC North.

Second-Half Outlook: Hope that Bo Nix can take his play up a notch (or two) to make them legitimate Super Bowl contenders in January

Very rarely does a team's fortune in one-score games carry over (good or bad) from season to season the way that the Broncos have. Even with Nix struggling for the majority of the season, they are a seven-win team in full control of their destiny. The defense remains elite, and if Nix can figure out a way to start challenging downfield more, there's no reason they can't find their way back to the AFC Championship game again this season. Even with the Daiyan Henley deal falling through, there's little reason to doubt this defense.

Second-Half Outlook: Get healthy on both sides of the ball and hope that their slow start doesn't keep them out of the playoffs come January

Despite coming into the season as the overwhelming Super Bowl favorites, the Rams haven't been healthy enough to reach their ceiling. While there's still time for that to happen, Puka Nacua's trip to Injured Reserve is a tough blow to absorb, especially with Davante Adams still a few weeks away from returning. The NFC is loaded, and even for as talented as Los Angeles is, they face an uphill battle to make the playoffs. We'll see if quarterback Matthew Stafford can elevate his play without his two best receivers. Their season might depend on it.

Second-Half Outlook: Get healthy at quarterback and hope their slow start doesn't keep them out of the playoffs come January (like the Rams)

If you're comparing the Rams' and Seahawks' schedules down the stretch, Seattle has the clear advantage, especially with both teams holding the same record. As noted before, the NFC is loaded, and barring a second-half collapse from the 49ers, the division is all but out of reach. Quarterback play has been an issue for most of the season, so the Seahawks have to hope that when Sam Darnold returns, he's playing multiple levels above what he was when he went out.

Second-Half Outlook: Fight off the Bengals in the AFC North and hope that their older roster doesn't wear down in December

In my estimation, the Steelers have looked considerably better than expected. Aaron Rodgers is clearly a 43-year-old quarterback on the back end of his career, but the defense has not seen a drop-off with the departure of former head coach Mike Tomlin. On paper, this is a fringe playoff team, but following a slow start to the season, they've rounded into form and have looked like a true playoff contender. The bigger question is about their ceiling, but for now, they're locked into a battle to repeat as AFC North champs.

Second-Half Outlook: Wait for Micah Parsons' return and hope that their weaknesses don't cost them in the end

Following a brutal start to the season, the Packers have rounded into form. The scary part- it's been without their star pass rusher. The offensive line might still be leaning "makeshift," but with Jordan Love playing the way he has, it hasn't mattered until Sunday. Christian Watson and Matthew Golden have been the league's most explosive receiving tandem, on top of it. Parsons' return will be big, but following a loss to the Vikings, their backs are going to be against the wall over these final seven games. "Thanksgiving Eve" becomes as close to a "must-win" game as the Packers have had this year.

Second-Half Outlook: Continue to build on a surprising season and hope to hang around in the Wild Card race into late December

Even if their chances of making the playoffs shrink with every loss, the Browns have been one of the better stories in football so far in 2026. First-year head coach Todd Monken has done a nice job, and their high-round rookies are looking like hits. There's plenty of young talent on this team, and even if they can't finish the job with a Wild Card berth, it's hard not to see this season as a success. The future is bright in Cleveland, especially if they can find a quarterback.

Second-Half Outlook: Continue to do exactly what they are doing and hold onto first place

Without any other context to the season, it would be easy to say that the Giants have arrived ahead of schedule. Add in some key injuries to players like quarterback Jaxson Dart and edge rusher Brian Burns, and their hot start is even more impressive. New York has started three quarterbacks this season, and now has J.J. McCarthy playing the best football of his career. All things considered, this season should be considered a success no matter what, but even after a disappointing loss on Thursday night, they are well on pace to win the NFC East for the first time in over a decade.

Second-Half Outlook: Survive long enough to get back some defensive reinforcements and win the division

It hasn't always been pretty, and despite a rollercoaster ride for the offense, the Panthers held onto the division lead on Sunday with a big win in New Orleans. Bryce Young's productivity and efficiency have fallen off a cliff since late October, but this offense still has plenty of weapons. Getting back both starting cornerbacks and keeping Jaelan Phillips will be key to getting this defense back on track. Even if they don't look improved over last season, the rest of the division might be worse. At this point, the goal should be finding a way to finish over .500.

Second-Half Outlook: Survive without Drake Maye and hope that his ankle injury isn't season-ending

Originally, I would have said that they simply need to put these last two games behind them and figure out how to win the Wild Card. The Maye injury changes everything, and the early reports are that he might miss the rest of the regular season. If that's the case, the Patriots are in serious trouble. Even if he misses the next four-to-five games, New England might be in trouble. Injuries have plagued them all year, but Maye was one of the only good things going for this group.

Second-Half Outlook: Cling to their slim playoff hopes and pray that Christian Parker can fix the defense

The Cowboys remain on the fringe of the playoff picture, but the Giants' loss on Thursday night opened the door for Dallas to get back into the race. The offense has been somewhat inconsistent, but the defense will ultimately dictate their season. The talent is there, but so far, the entire product simply hasn't come together as hoped. Following a quiet trade deadline, it feels like Brian Schottenheimer and his staff are quietly fighting for their jobs, especially with a desperate owner in Jerry Jones. Sunday's 46-40 loss at home was not a great step in the right direction.

Second-Half Outlook: Enjoy the ride with Fernando Mendoza over the final eight games of the season

With last Tuesday's deadline trade of Kirk Cousins, it's Mendoza's team down the stretch. Following a 3-0 start, it was easy for Raiders fans to believe that maybe they could be a "surprise" playoff team in 2026, but as the season has played out, reality has struck. This can still be a successful season, and assuming Mendonza is ready, I would already classify the year as a success. That said, how Mendonza develops on the field will matter heading into the offseason and 2027.

Second-Half Outlook: Figure out the passing game and ride a top-tier defense to a division title

News broke on Sunday that quarterback Baker Mayfield is dealing with a leg injury, and his status for Week 11 is in doubt. Considering they are facing one of the hottest teams in football, in Detroit, that's a tough ask for an undrafted free agent. The Bucs have a Super Bowl-caliber defense, but unless they can marry the passing game with a dangerous rushing attack, it's hard to envision many scenarios where they can string wins together. Although they are just one game back, they'll need to find more consistency down the stretch.

Second-Half Outlook: Hope that it's not too late to get back into the Wild Card picture

On one side, the Browns' last-minute win might have saved their season (at least for the time being). For the Texans, their season is on life support with a limited ceiling, unless they win out. The AFC's final Wild Card spot is still gettable, but with the Browns leading that race and Houston's head-to-head loss, DeMeco Ryans and company have their backs against the wall. It'll likely take a 7-1 finish, with games remaining against the Steelers, Jaguars, and Packers over the final two months of the season. Good luck.

Second-Half Outlook: Hope that a second-half run is possible and avoid big changes in the offseason

It's been back-to-back one-score games for the Saints coming out of their bye week. Unfortunately, the more important of the two games is the one they lost. Although they'll have another crack at the Falcons next month, they are 0-2 within the division and 1-4 in the conference. Barring a successful run against the Bears, Bengals, and Packers coming up, the outlook for the remainder of their season appears bleak. Ownership has already turned up the heat following a slow start, so things better improve soon or changes could be coming.

Second-Half Outlook: Hope that Jacoby Brissett can get you back in the Wild Card race

The back end of the AFC Wild Card picture is still wide open, especially with the Patriots struggling over the last few games. That said, the Ravens are banged up and on their fourth quarterback of the season. Despite injuries to players like Lamar Jackson, the Ravens are still surviving. If all goes well, he can make it back before the end of the season, but a lot of that will depend on how well the Ravens can do until the middle-to-end of December.

Second-Half Outlook: Evaluate the coaching staff and keep quarterback Jayden Daniels healthy

Thursday night's win mathematically keeps them in the divisional race, but barring a serious collapse down the stretch, Washington's season is still all but over. At this point, figuring out who is worth keeping around for the future should be the primary goal. Head coach Dan Quinn and his coaching staff are fighting for their coaching lives, so we'll see how it goes. Outside of being in the NFC South, the Commanders might be in the right division to make a comeback happen, but the margin for error will be extremely small from here on out.

Second-Half Outlook: Get back to Weeks 3 through 5's offensive production and take a run at the division

Each loss makes that more difficult, but in the weakest division in football, nothing is impossible. Really, though, the offense struggling has been a big issue for this entire team. Michael Penix looked good after returning from injury, but his last few games have left a lot to be desired. This has always been the concern with this roster. Although they are far from out of the playoff race, it's going to take quite a run for them to make that happen.

Second-Half Outlook: Just survive with an eye towards April's quarterback class

Injuries have completely derailed what has otherwise been a quality rebuilding season. With Jacoby Brissett in Baltimore and Gardner Minshew done for the season, the offense's ceiling is bleak, especially without Michael Wilson. This team needs a long-term solution at quarterback, and unless rookie Carson Beck takes the world by storm, that'll be the case come March and April. First-year head coach Mike LaFleur has done a nice job, but there's still plenty of work to be done in the future.

Second-Half Outlook: Evaluate the coaching staff and prepare for plenty of changes ahead

One thing you learn over time during Black Monday is that surprises happen every year. Typically, when a team fires a general manager midseason with a regime already in question, the head coach and his staff don't survive past the regular season. My gut tells me that's what happens here, but only time will tell. The Colts have needed a rebuild for a few years, and firing Chris Ballard should jumpstart the process. Like most teams at the bottom of our rankings, it's a wait-and-see approach heading into the offseason.

Second-Half Outlook: Prove enough down the stretch to give the coaching staff a third season

Barring an unexpected turnaround over the second half of the season, it feels unlikely that the Jets will continue to hang with the same coaching staff. Head coach Aaron Glenn is a good leader on paper, but this group has not melded the way most expected. Although they might not have a Top 3 pick when all is said and done, they'll likely have three selections in the Top 10. That will be extremely attractive if the Jets decide to make a change. For now, trying to save jobs is all that's going to be worth watching.

Second-Half Outlook: Survive the season and wait for the fallout

Although things didn't fall apart last season as they should have, the bottom has completely collapsed in 2026. It started with a few losses in a row after a 2-0 start, but once Jalen Hurts was placed on Injured Reserve with blood clots in his lungs, the ceiling on this season has totally disappeared. This group has plenty of questions moving forward, but general manager Howie Roseman is one of the best. Right now, it's just about surviving the final stretch of games and making some tough decisions when the offseason arrives.

Second-Half Outlook: Can the Chargers avoid a regime change after a disastrous winless start to the season

For a while, it felt like everyone was waiting for the Chargers to figure things out one week and hit their stride. September and October came and went without a win, and now, heading into mid-November, their season is over. Despite that, they didn't make a single (official) trade, which was confounding, to say the least. Considering what they invested in Jim Harbaugh when he was hired three offseasons ago, cutting bait won't be easy, but it also won't be easy to excuse how poorly this season has gone. There's plenty to monitor heading into January.

Second-Half Outlook: Figure out if Cam Ward is the quarterback of the future

2026 has been nothing short of a disappointment for the Titans. What was once just a slow start turned into serious questions about the future. Now that Jeffery Simmons is in Chicago, the focus is solely on the future. The first question they must answer is whether Ward is their quarterback of the future. Through nine weeks, it hasn't been pretty, but there's simply too much talent for him to be this bad. The final eight games of the season will go a long way in determining whether or not they'll be in the quarterback market come March and April.

Second-Half Outlook: Keep on building, even without key veteran pieces

Last week was a rough one on the injury front for the Dolphins. Their playoff hopes are all but dead, but this season has never realistically been about anything more than building for the future. Quarterback Malik Willis is down for at least the next four games, and veteran defensive tackle Zach Sieler is done for the year. At this point, Miami must keep looking toward the future, and all of that depends on the young core they are trying to build.

#2667. Rangers lose star goaltender Igor Shesterkin for season with lower-body injury; what's next for New York?

If not listed, please contact your TV provider.

New York Rangers goaltender Igor Shesterkin will miss the remainder of the season with a lower-body injury, the team announced on Saturday.

Shesterkin suffered an apparent leg injury in the Rangers' loss to the Washington Capitals on Friday night as his right leg slid awkwardly into the post while scrambling to get back in position. Shesterkin fell to the ice immediately, and he needed assistance to get down the tunnel.

Prior to that loss, the Rangers were off to a terrific 4-1-0 start, and Shesterkin was a driving force behind that success. In just five appearances, Shesterkin posted 3.90 goals saved above average with a .900 high-danger save percentage, according to Natural Stat Trick.

The 2022 Vezina Trophy winner, Shesterkin has put up sparkling numbers since he entered the NHL in 2019-20. In 330 games, Shesterkin boasts a .917 save percentage, a 2.51 GAA and 22 shutouts. Over the last three full seasons from 2023-26, Shesterkin ranked third in goals saved above average with 45.4. Only Connor Hellebuyck and Andrei Vasilevskiy were better in that category.

Shesterkin was a big reason why the Rangers felt they could bounce back from a disappointing 2025-26 season, and losing the star goaltender puts a huge dent in the team's playoff hopes. It doesn't help that backup goalie Joonas Korpisalo is also hurt.

Dylan Garand replaced Shesterkin on Friday night, and Spencer Martin will be recalled from the AHL after recovering from his own injury. With the Rangers playing well early, it wouldn't be a shock to see them explore better replacement options for Shesterkin.

New York won't be able to replace Shesterkin's impact because he's one of the five best goalies in the world. However, the team should be able to upgrade its current goaltending situation, which is a fairly low bar to clear.

First, there are unsigned veterans still on the open market in Petr Mrazek and James Reimer. Neither one was great last season -- hence their availability at the moment -- Reimer and Mrazek could provide a level of stability in the crease that the Rangers simply don't have right now.

New York could also explore trade possibilities, and Minnesota Wild netminder Filip Gustavsson could be a solution there. Jesper Wallstedt is the future of the crease in Minnesota, making Gustavsson more of a luxury. Would the Wild send Gustavsson to New York in exchange for some draft capital it could use to acquire a center?

The one snag in a potential Gustavsson deal is his contract. Gustavsson is in the first year of a deal that pays him $6.8 million over the next five seasons. That's a big commitment for a player who will become a backup when Shesterkin returns.

Obviously, Connor Hellebuyck has been on the trade market for months now, but that trade wouldn't make sense for the Rangers. Hellebuyck is on an expensive long-term deal, and New York would have $20 million tied up in goalies if they made that move, not to mention the astronomical acquisition cost.

However, if you'll allow me to get creative here, it's no secret that the Florida Panthers have pursed Hellebuyck. What if the Panthers traded Jacob Markstrom -- just acquired in the offseason -- to the Rangers in order to make room for Hellebuyck?

Markstrom does have a 20-team no-trade list, so the question is whether New York would be one of his 11 approved teams. Florida flipping Markstrom so quickly seems like a long shot, but the team has taken plenty of big swings in recent history.

#2666. Open Thread: San Antonio Spurs kick off their annual “Season of Giving”

Each year at this time, the San Antonio Spurs hosts a series of events designed to support the community. Through outreach, food distribution, and gift-giving the organization invites families to partake in a series of Spurs holiday traditions.

"The San Antonio Spurs are brightening the holiday season for local families through community-centered initiatives and player engagements as part of the annual "NBA Season of Giving," a five-week celebration running from mid-November through December when NBA teams give back by supporting and uplifting youth, families and organizations in their communities."

On Monday, November 16, the Spurs hosted families from local community organizations for a Thanksgiving-themed dinner at Frost Bank Center. Spurs staff volunteers, Hype Squad and Coyote served dinner, followed by an on-court activity for the youngsters participating in the evening.

They were joined by players Luke Kornet, Jayden Quinatance, Tarris Reed, Jr. and David Jones Garcia.

Said Patricia Mejia, Chief Impact and Inclusion Officer at SS&E,

"The holidays are a time to come together and care for one another, and we want families across San Antonio to feel that support this season. Through Season of Giving, our players, staff and partners can help ease some of the pressures families face and create opportunities to enjoy the holidays together."

The Spurs Season of Giving continues Wednesday with an H-E-B Thanksgiving food distribution.

#2665. Jerry Jones might be ready to fire Cowboys coach after latest comments

The NFL season is quickly turning into a nightmare for the Dallas Cowboys, and owner Jerry Jones may be considering a major coaching change following the team's latest disappointing performance.

After a historic defensive collapse against the San Francisco 49ers, questions are mounting about the job security of defensive coordinator Christian Parker.

The Cowboys suffered a heartbreaking 46-40 loss to San Francisco on Sunday in Week 10 of the 2026 NFL season. However, the final score only tells part of the story, as Dallas' defense delivered one of the worst performances in franchise history.

The Cowboys allowed 584 total yards and surrendered three touchdowns of 60 or more yards against the 49ers. It was the most net yards Dallas has ever allowed in a home game in franchise history.

MORE: Browns end 63-year drought in win over Texans in NFL Week 10

Nov 15, 2026; Arlington, Texas, USA; San Francisco 49ers running back Christian McCaffrey (23) rushes for a touchdown against the Dallas Cowboys at AT&T Stadium. Mandatory Credit: Kevin Jairaj-Imagn Images

Following the loss, Jones made his weekly appearance on 105.3 The Fan in Dallas, where he was asked whether Parker's role could change ahead of the team's Week 11 matchup against the Tennessee Titans.

"We're talking about that, but I'm not going to talk about it here. But we are talking about those things," Jones said.

Those comments certainly suggest that changes could be under consideration, especially with the Cowboys' defense continuing to struggle.

Dallas currently ranks last in the NFL in yards allowed per game, surrendering 393.8. The team also sits last in rushing defense, allowing 154.1 yards per game, while ranking 30th in points allowed at 28.2 per contest.

For a team with playoff expectations, those numbers are simply unacceptable.

MORE: Rob Gronkowski doesn't hold back in criticism of Cowboys' Week 10 performance

Jul 29, 2026; Oxnard, CA, USA; Dallas Cowboys defensive coordinator Christian Parker (left) with head coach Brian Schottenheimer at training camp at River Ridge Playing Fields. Mandatory Credit: Kirby Lee-Imagn Images

Parker is in his first season as Dallas' defensive coordinator, but his unit has struggled to find consistency throughout the campaign.

Head coach Brian Schottenheimer was also asked about Parker's job security on Monday. Rather than publicly backing his coordinator, Schottenheimer offered a cautious response.

"We're still in the process of going through all the film and evaluation of where we stand," Schottenheimer said.

The Cowboys are now 4-6 and desperately need to turn things around. They'll host the 1-8 Tennessee Titans on Sunday in Week 11.

Whether Parker gets another opportunity remains to be seen, but Jones' latest comments make it clear that difficult conversations are taking place behind the scenes. After Sunday's defensive disaster, his future in Dallas could be in serious jeopardy.

#2664. Steelers host former Chiefs cornerback for workout

The Pittsburgh Steelers are hosting former Kansas City Chiefs cornerback Nazeeh Johnson for a workout on Tuesday, per Jordan Schultz.

Johnson was drafted in the seventh round of the 2022 NFL Draft by the Chiefs out of Marshall. He appeared in 11 games as a rookie, but missed all of 2023 with an injury and was placed on IR in July. He was part of the Chiefs' 2024 Super Bowl-winning team, appearing in 16 games and registering 56 tackles and three pass breakups. He found himself on IR again ahead of the 2025 season and appeared in just two games. He signed with the Tennessee Titans this past offseason, but was suspended for the first six games of the year due to violating the NFL's policy against PEDs, and he was waived in early September.

The Steelers have an obvious need at cornerback after Ja'Marr Chase torched their secondary for 231 receiving yards. Should the Steelers add Johnson to the roster, it could be the beginning of the end for Asante Samuel Jr, who was credited with giving up five receptions for 135 yards against Cincinnati, per Next Gen Stats.

#2662. Wizards hammered by Memphis Grizzlies for 8th straight loss

The Wizards played 24 good minutes against the Memphis Grizzlies. Unfortunately, the game lasted 48 minutes. Their worst 12 minutes came in the third quarter. They started the period up 10 and finished it down 14, courtesy of a 42-18 beatdown by Cameron Boozer, Zach Edey, and the rest of the Grizzlies.

Fifteen games into the season where they hoped to compete again, the Wizards have a 4-11 record, and they're currently on an eight-game losing streak. It's starting to feel like last year. And the year before. And the year before.

If you missed this one, a) congratulations, and b) here are a few tidbits to illustrate how this one went:

Washington's defensive game plan was built around defensive indifference — they were going to concede three-point shots to Boozer. He missed his first five…and then made seven of his last eight. Boozer finished with a career-high 29 points,.

Edey dominated Washington's Twin Towers lineup, notching 23 points (on 10-15 shooting) and 10 rebounds in just 21 minutes.

Javon Small had his first career double-double — 12 points, 12 assists.

The Grizzlies shot 64.2% (effective field goal percentage) and rebounded 42.9% of their misses.

That's the second consecutive game the Wizards gave up a 60+% efg and an opponent offensive rebound rate above 40%. I don't know for sure because it probably never occurred to anyone to track this combination of stats, but I suspect it's exceedingly rare to do both in a single game. I mean, it never occurred to me to pay attention until the Wizards did it Sunday night. It never occurred to me they'd do the same thing on Monday night.

By the way, the Wizards entered the game ranked 28th in strength of schedule adjusted scoring margin. They probably can't fall in the rankings — they're ahead of the Milwaukee Bucks and Charlotte Hornets. But man…this is the team that's supposed to be trying to compete.

The problem is kinda everything. Trae Young and Anthony Davis are supposed to be the bedrock. The youngsters are supposed to be making some version of The Leap. Except, Young and Davis have been up and down. Both have exhibited problems with effort and focus (more on that in the notebook section). And none of the kids are leaping.

I mean, except Kyshawn George, if you squint just enough to miss all the crazy turnovers and dumb fouls.

While I don't think Xs and Os are a problem, there's a disconnect somewhere that shows up in the team's effort, execution, and ability to maintain focus for a full 48. Last night, for example, the team looked good for half the game. In the second half, they got pummeled, and no one showed a bit of fight. They all just kinda let it happen.

Brian Keefe was frustrated enough by the Houston debacle Sunday night that he publicly challenged their effort. That's a sign of desperation — a coach whose message isn't breaking through. And then they got thoroughly outplayed by Memphis.

Six minutes into the game, Memphis had six offensive rebounds. The Wizards had five defensive rebounds. For the game, it was 17 offensive boards for Memphis, and 20 defense rebounds for Washington.

What the hell was that? In the first quarter, the Grizzlies had a quasi-fast break led by Javon Small. Four Wizards were back. Trae Young looked like he was going to pick up ball, when he inexplicably gestured to Bilal Coulibaly to take ball, and then abruptly switched out onto a Grizzlies player on the wing. That gave Small a free run at the basket (Coulibaly was standing under the basket when the "pick him up" suggestion arrived). Coulibaly fouled late, and Small got a three-point play. I rewatched the play 10-12 times, and I still have no idea why Young didn't just pick up Small.

Late in the first quarter, Young had a thoroughly disgusting shot attempt — a 29-foot heave with nine seconds still on the shot clock, and a plenty of space to drive or make a good play.

Washington's defensive indifference meant that Boozer had more firts quarter three-point attempts in Grizzlies history.

Egregious effort from Anthony Davis midway through the third quarter. He tried for a steal and missed. And then…instead of hustling back into the action, he stood around on the perimeter watching and leaving his teammates to defend 5-0n-4. Memphis got an open three.

Keefe is trying a tighter and older rotation. Last night, they played nine while trying to compete — a nine that replaced Bub Carrington with Khris Middleton.

Another effort issue with Davis. He tried a shot, fell down, and didn't get the call he wanted from the refs. Instead of getting up and sprinting back, he lollygagged on the floor complaining and never got back across halfcourt. In the five-on-four, Boozer got a wide open three.

Defensive communication issue — in the third quarter, Davis dropped off Boozer at the three-point line and drifted down into the paint. No one picked him up, and a few seconds later, Boozer got a wide open three, which he converted into his sixth made triple.

I have two notes about Kyshawn George fouls in the fourth quarter. The first came early and was utterly pointless — he grabbed Cam Spencer on an Iverson cut for no discernible reason. The second came midway through the period when the Wizards seeemd to be cutting into the Memphis lead. For no reason I could determine, George grabbed Cedric Coward and sent him to the free throw line. It was dumb, pointless, and momentum-killing.

Edey was impressive. He scored comfortably on Davis and Sarr. He big-boyed George for an offensive rebound and foul on the putback. He's massive, strong, and skilled — great touch with both hands.

Edey had a great nope against George. George made a nice dribble-drive attack in transition, shook Spencer and seemed ready to make a run straight to the rim for a bucket and maybe a free throw. Except, the 7-3 Edey was in the way. George came to a screeching half, fired a crosscourt pass, which ultimately resulted in Young driving and missing a floater.

The Wizards led by as much as 12 in the first half…and trailed by as much as 20 in the second half.

Against the Wizards, you're never more than two passes from an open three.

Below are the four factors that decide wins and losses in basketball — shooting (efg), rebounding (offensive rebounds), ball handling (turnovers), fouling (free throws made).

eFG% (effective field goal percentage, which accounts for the three-point shot)

TOV% (turnover percentage — turnovers divided by possessions)

FTM/FGA (free throws made divided by field goal attempts)

PPA is my overall production metric, which credits players for things they do that help a team win (scoring, rebounding, playmaking, defending) and dings them for things that hurt (missed shots, turnovers, bad defense, fouls).

PPA is a per possession metric designed for larger data sets. In small sample sizes, the numbers can get weird. In PPA, 100 is average, higher is better and replacement level is 45. For a single game, replacement level isn't much use, and I reiterate the caution about small samples sometimes producing weird results.

POSS is the number of possessions each player was on the floor in this game.

ORTG = offensive rating, which is points produced per individual possessions x 100. League average so far this season is listed in the Four Factors table above. Points produced is not the same as points scored. It includes the value of assists and offensive rebounds, as well as sharing credit when receiving an assist.

USG = offensive usage rate. Average is 20%. Median last season was 17.7%.

ORTG and USG are versions of stats created by former Wizards assistant coach Dean Oliver and modified by me. ORTG is an efficiency measure that accounts for the value of shooting, offensive rebounds, assists and turnovers. USG includes shooting from the floor and free throw line, offensive rebounds, assists and turnovers.

+PTS = "Plus Points" is a measure of the points gained or lost by each player based on their efficiency in this game compared to league average efficiency on the same number of possessions. A player with an offensive rating (points produced per possession x 100) of 100 who uses 20 possessions would produce 20 points. If the league average efficiency is 115, the league — on average — would produced 23.0 points in the same 20 possessions. So, the player in this hypothetical would have a +PTS score of -3.0.

Players are sorted by total production in the game.

#2661. Bears WR Rome Odunze pinpoints where he needs to improve most

The Chicago Bears offense has been dynamic all season, but they do not have a top-tier superstar at any skill position, rather they're led by a collection of high-level talent, especially at wide receiver.

While Luther Burden III has established himself as one that many believe is the team's No. 1 option, the Bears still have former first-round pick Rome Odunze, who has plenty of big-play ability but has struggled with consistency dating back to last season.

This season, Odunze has 32 receptions, 528 yards, and just one touchdown, while being targeted 52 times, and he trails just Burden and Colston Loveland in most categories. During an appearance on "Up & Adams," Odunze admitted that he knows he has to play with more consistently to improve his game in the offense.

"The biggest thing for me is just being consistent," Odunze said. "I feel like I have great flashes and some good consistency throughout the season. But the biggest thing for me is making all the plays that come my way, consistently. There's a lot of great players on this offense, so many people that can do great things with the ball in their hands and make incredible plays. The opportunities aren't going to come like 15-20 targets a game, for me, I just want to make the most of every play that comes my way and be consistent with that."

The Bears having plenty of weapons on their offense does mean that there are limited opportunities for everyone, and Odunze would benefit greatly from showing an uptick in his consistency. If Odunze and Burden both become consistently reliable and productive at wide receiver, it could unlock yet another level to the Bears offense, especially through the air.

#2658. Hutchinson ruled out for season after celebration injury

Detroit Lions defensive end Aidan Hutchinson will miss the rest of the NFL season after sustaining a serious knee injury while celebrating.

Hutchinson, 26, jumped in the air after bringing down New England Patriots quarterback Drake Maye in the first quarter of the Lions' 35-10 win in Munich.

The 2022 second overall pick fell to the ground shortly after landing, clutching his right knee.

Hutchinson walked to the sideline after medical treatment on the field but did not return to the game - and has torn his anterior cruciate ligament.

It is the second season-ending injury of Hutchinson career - but Lions head coach Dan Campbell has no plans to stop his players from expressing themselves.

"I hate it. I think we all understand what it is, and let's be smart, but no, I'm not gonna say 'nobody celebrates any more'," Campbell said.

"The number of moves that I've seen 'Hutch' make and the number of plyometrics, explosive movements, the spins, the one-leg lateral movements, lateral balances... it was one of those things, man."

This was the sixth regular-season NFL game to be played in Germany and the third to be held at Bayern Munich's Allianz Arena.

The Lions' win means they are top of the NFC North and have the second-best record in the conference.

Hutchinson is regarded as one of the premier pass rushers in the NFL, and is currently tied for 13th in the league with six sacks this season.

Campbell is confident Hutchinson will come back stronger on his return from the injury setback.

"He's such a phenomenal player, an impact player, but more importantly he's an unbelievable team-mate and he's one of our captains," Campbell added.

"What a hell of a year he was having. He's just improved every year and to come off the injury he had [in 2024].

"This guy will overcome this and he will come back better than he was. It's just the way he is, it's the way he's wired."

Drake Maye led the New England Patriots to Super Bowl 60, where they lost to the Seattle Seahawks [Getty Images]

Maye reportedly sustained a fractured ankle during the tackle Hutchinson was celebrating, so the Patriots will be concerned the quarterback could miss the remainder of the season too.

Head coach Mike Vrabel confirmed Maye had remained in Germany, telling Boston radio station WEEI the 24-year-old stayed "out of caution".

After being beaten by the Seattle Seahawks in the 2026 Super Bowl, the Patriots are second in the AFC East having won five and lost five this season.

Their chances of reaching the playoffs will likely be reliant on securing a wildcard place as the Buffalo Bills currently top the division with an 8-1 record.

#2656. Under new chief marketing officer James Ruth, the Dallas Mavericks are telling a fresh story

A blue rotary phone sits on a stand. On its dial, a badge with the number 11. One by one, fans from across the metroplex — fathers and sons, aunts and uncles, young and old — step up and dial 1-1.

"I have a son that adores you," one fan says. "And we love your game, and we hope you have a phenomenal year, and you tear it up this year for the Mavericks."

They welcome Kyrie Irving back home. They thank him, congratulate him and motivate him as he returns to the American Airlines Center after more than 600 days away. After a long road of blood, sweat, and recovery.

"Kyrie Irving, you're an inspiration. Setbacks happen, but you can't stay down. You gotta keep getting back up, and that's what you're showing the world. And for that, we'll always be grateful for your leadership. You'll always have a special place in my heart."

When they speak into the phone, they speak to him like family. Their uncle, son, brother, friend. It's a simple video produced by the Mavericks content team, but it speaks to the connection between the franchise and its fans.

There is a new story being told in Dallas, and if you haven't taken notice, it's time you did.

"What makes sports an amazing thing is the idea that it's a community connector," James Ruth, Dallas Mavericks Chief Marketing Officer, said in a recent exclusive interview with Mavs Moneyball. "We have these opportunities to create sort of collective moments, and what an awesome thing to be able to do that in a city like Dallas, Texas. To serve as a sort of connected device. And oh, by the way, we get to watch players like Cooper and Kai and PJ and all these others. It's an amazing thing."

For Ruth, who was hired in July after serving as CMO for the Tampa Bay Buccaneers for the last three years, this is a return to Texas. He led the launch of MLS club Austin FC during the pandemic and did his undergraduate work at SMU. Now in Dallas, Ruth leads a talented group of producers and creators to tell the story of the Mavericks and the fans that support them. The rotary phone video, "From Dallas with Love", is one of an already long list of pieces that have captured the attention of the fan base. Spend just a short time on the Mavericks social media comment sections, and you'll see this revitalized content team isn't going unnoticed.

"We have these opportunities to create sort of collective moments, and what an awesome thing to be able to do that in a city like Dallas, Texas. To serve as a sort of connected device."

Team media content isn't new, of course. But in seeing what Ruth and his staff have put out in this young season, it is immediately apparent that the Mavericks' story is being framed with new eyes and new energy for a new era. Take, for instance, a series of clips that have popped up after the team's first two NBA Cup games. The experience is visceral. It gives you the highlights from a 116-111 win over the Houston Rockets, but it also puts you in the stands. In the above clip a static camera from a fan's view hyper-cuts the climax of the stadium roar with the calm before the storm. We already know the outcome, but reliving the moments, the push and pull of the theater of sport, is what draws you in and makes you want to be at the American Airlines Center the next time the magic happens. And you'll notice it isn't just telling the story of the game, but also the story of those working behind the scenes, and the sensory connection and contribution fans bring to a win.

"We want to get back to the fans understanding the role with this team, which is: y'all are part of it. You are all creating this experience at AAC. And that's a thing where players pick up on it."

This inclusiveness is an intentional and impactful choice. It is no secret that the last 20 months have often felt tense between Mavericks fans and the organization. We're barely one year removed from the arena echoing with chants to fire the team's general manager. That road created distance between the fan base and leadership. For the last six months, team governor Patrick Dumont took steps to mend some of that – to start, by bringing in Masai Ujiri to run basketball operations. In his opening remarks, he made clear his objective was bringing joy back to the fans. He's now revamped the organization by hiring Mike Schmitz to help lead basketball decision-making, and Dusty May as head coach, who, to start the season, has been something of a breath of fresh air in strength and leadership.

In bringing Ruth into the fold to tell the team's story, the team has someone with experience in franchise transitions: in introducing Austin FC to the city for the very first time and in taking over the Tampa Bay Buccaneers brand just after Tom Brady retired. Whether that's coincidence or not, Ruth and his team have a wealth of experience in helping fans and franchises navigate new eras. And his latest opportunity in Dallas invigorates him.

"I think the opportunity that we have with the Mavericks is arguably the best opportunity in North American sports, period, full stop," he said about what drew him to the role this summer. He quickly understood what the team needed to do in "making sure that the Mavericks are always creating a world where players, fans, front office, they all feel like they're part of the same ecosystem."

"It's all getting to this North Star idea of how are we blurring the lines between players and fans. Because when we blur that line, everybody feels more ownership and engagement."

Some of that connection also comes through seeing players in new and different ways — not just who they are on the court, but who they are as people. The team has done plenty of this in the past and has highlighted their work in the community. In this season's Home & Away series, fans get to see what made the player who they are today. Giving a voice to the player beyond their reach on the floor.

The season is still developing. With so many moving parts and new pieces, on the floor and off, expectations on where the team could go were relatively quiet. Their surprising record in a very tough early schedule injected even greater energy into the fan base and team. Winning does wonders for the outlook of a franchise. Inevitably, just like the team's most recent road trip, there will be valleys ahead. Cooper Flagg and many of the key pieces on the team are still learning and evolving as players, individually and together. And that's why, for Ruth and his team, it is important to fortify the relationship and continue following their North Star in the way they capture everything that happens ahead.

"It's the power of fandom. When you make sure that you are spending as much time on what's happening on the court as you are on what's happening in the stands…if you walk too far away from what's happening in the stands, you start to walk away from what I believe is the sort of core value proposition to sports, which is that connective device."

It remains to be seen where this season and beyond will go. But maybe now this team and its fans are ready to write a new chapter.

#2654. Cowboys coach Brian Schottenheimer again declines to support DC Christian Parker after struggles, brutal loss to 49ers

Brian Schottenheimer, at least publicly, isn't backing his defensive coordinator.

The Cowboys head coach didn't directly support defensive coordinator Christian Parker on Monday, one day after a brutal showing from the Dallas defense in its 46-40 loss to the San Francisco 49ers.

Instead, he said everything is still under review.

"We're still working through the process, talking to the guys is the first step," Schottenheimer said, via The Dallas Morning News. "At the end of the day, there's a lot of things that we need to clean up as a football team. That starts with me."

The 49ers racked up 584 yards of offense and averaged 9.4 yards per play in the win on Sunday. They ran for 214 yards, too, and put up 29 points and 340 yards in the second half alone. It was simply an offensive clinic that the Cowboys couldn't stop time and time again.

The 584 yards that Dallas allowed was the most they've allowed in a home game in franchise history.

Schottenheimer said after the game that he thought the defense was "unacceptable," and he called the tackling "atrocious."

"At the end of the day, we tackled like s**t in the second half," he said.

Dallas' defensive issues are nothing new. They've been a problem all season, and it's led to louder and louder calls to make a change at defensive coordinator. Parker is in his first season in the role, which also marks his first coordinator job in the NFL.

Though he declined to support Parker again on Monday, Schottenheimer did not say he was going to make a change.

"I'm not saying that," he said. "I'm saying we're still in the process of going through all the film and evaluation of where we stand today."

Perhaps more importantly, Cowboys owner Jerry Jones did back Parker on Sunday afternoon.

"Again, it's what it is," Jones said postgame. "He's a young coach in his first year of coordinating and calling the plays. So you have to say that you would hope you could win games like the last that we've lost.

"I'll weigh his early times. I've been with teams that had some pretty good coordinators on defense that ended up winning Super Bowls."

But instead of following Jones' lead, Schottenheimer said simply that they are "taking a deep dive" and "looking at everything."

During his weekly appearance on 105.3 The Fan in Dallas, all Jones would say is that Parker's position has come up.

"We're talking about that, but I'm not going to talk about it here," Jones said. "But we are talking about those things."

The Cowboys are still in the playoff hunt despite their 4-6 record, thanks to a rough NFC East. They are only two games behind the New York Giants. They'll take on the Tennessee Titans next weekend. But the Cowboys haven't won a Super Bowl since the 1995 season, and this team doesn't appear capable of ending that streak.

The frustration that fans feel, vice president Stephen Jones said, is being felt internally, too.

"I certainly understand their frustration because there's no doubt that we're frustrated," the younger Jones said on 105.3 The Fan. "We feel like the way we're playing ball right now is unacceptable. Our fans certainly deserve better."

Whether the outcry and issues on defense result in a change at defensive coordinator before the end of the season, however, is still anybody's guess.

#2650. Patriots margin of error ‘basically at zero’ after loss to Lions

Even though they are still 5-5 and only one spot outside of the playoff picture, the New England Patriots' season is at a crossroads. Injury questions with none more consequential than Drake Maye's are one part of it, but so is the performance on the field.

The Patriots are heading into their Week 11 bye off a two-game losing streak, with neither of the contests particularly competitive. The message coming out of the locker room is therefore clear: get it together, or else.

"We have a seven-game stretch that we have to – the margin of error is basically at zero," said safety Kevin Byard after the Patriots' 35-10 defeat at the hands of the Detroit Lions on Sunday. "We have to find a way to string some wins together. We have to start playing together as a team, and it's going to start in practice. Honestly, I feel like we had a great week of preparation this week. We're just searching for answers right now."

The Patriots did not stand a chance against the Lions in Munich over the weekend. While one could play the "what if" game in regards to Maye exiting the contest after one series, fact is that neither the offense nor the defense looked particularly capable of, or at times even interested in, putting up a fight.

The end result was jarring. Not only were the Patriots out-scored by 25 points, they also were out-gained by a whopping 343 yards. Lions running back Jahmyr Gibbs by himself put up more yards (252) and touchdowns (2) than all of New England's offense did — despite playing just 69% of Detroit's offensive snaps.

Long story short, this was a total collapse. It was also one the team needs to quickly put behind itself in order to move forward.

Unsurprisingly, head coach Mike Vrabel was trying to instill a fresh mindset right after the game.

"We're 0-0," he said during his post-game presser. "We're heading into a bye. We have to get some things fixed and changed and corrected, and figure out ways to win as opposed to what we're doing right now, which is not giving ourselves enough of a change."

The first step in that process is making sure the locker room stays united, even though Maye reportedly missing extensive time will make for a challenging environment. For Byard, one of the team's captains, doing so will not start by any raw-raw gestures but with the performance put forward every day.

"We have to perform better," he said. "Bottom line in this league, talking, motivational speeches, getting guys up on the sideline, it means nothing if we're not playing well. We're not playing connected as a team. We're not playing complementary football. I would have bet my paycheck today that we wouldn't put that performance out there that we did today. It just sucks right now. We are in a bit of a slump, injuries are piling up. It's all type of things. But, obviously, going to a bye week, I'm going to take some time off, take my mind off of things and try to recharge."

The Patriots as a whole are in need of that. Whether they come out improved on the other side will be up to them, even though the circumstances are difficult.

#2648. The Lakers are an NBA title contender because Luka Doncic is completely out of control

I'm something of an expert on one-man teams. And the 2026-27 Los Angeles Lakers and Luka Doncic look like they're taking my theories to heart.

The Lakers didn't necessarily look like they would be a completely Luka-centric roster this season, and they did spend money and draft capital upgrading the team around him this offseason; they have a second scorer in Austin Reaves, and this is hardly the least-talented roster Doncic has ever had to play with. But he's just taken every bull by every horn and become the immovable center of a 12-2 Lakers team, and he singlehandedly makes them a contender to win the West. Yes, we're at that point.

Doncic is completely out of control this season. He's averaging 39.0 points per game and leading the league in all sorts of hilarious things: shot attempts, 3-point attempts, free-throw attempts. Basically anything that ends with "attempts," Luka is attempting it. And he's making it too, notably making 41 percent of his 3-pointers on over 13 attempts per game — if you don't intuitively understand how ridiculous that is, that's fine, let me spell it out:

If you make 41.3 percent of your 3-pointers, you inherently produce the best offense in NBA history simply as a function of points per 100 possessions. The only team that's ever done that as a team (with a normal 3-point line) is the 73-9 Golden State Warriors, but lots of players have shot at or above 41 percent. The problem is doing that at volume, but Doncic is almost doing it at over 13 threes per game, which is not supposed to be a thing; he's never shot that well in his career, nowhere near that actually, and so we'd expect some regression, but even a 38-39 percent-shooting Doncic at this kind of volume is going to bring a serious amount of points to the table.

And he's doing it with a pantheonic ball-hog season so far. In terms of the most one-man seasons in NBA history by usage rate, there are three seasons ever over 40 percent: 2016-17 Russell Westbrook is in a special category; he won the MVP and averaged a triple-double but also thought about his stats more than any player I've ever seen on a basketball court. 2018-19 James Harden is number two, when he threw down over 36 points per game on a Rockets team that had no other scoring to speak of … and then it's this Luka Doncic season.

Interestingly enough, he has the highest career usage rate of any player in NBA history, a function of how every team Doncic has ever been on has basically been built entirely around him. But getting and staying above 40 percent usage puts you in the Twilight Zone, where we have to start asking the hard questions: does this actually work?

The 2017 Westbrook team went 47-35 and the 2019 Harden team went 53-29. The Lakers are currently on pace to go, well … 70-12, which I don't expect will happen, but I truly believe these kinds of heliocentric experiments can and do work mathematically. And I think Luka's play this season absolutely makes the Lakers a serious contender, and perhaps one of the favorites — it is totally possible, even feasible, for a single player to carry an NBA team through the playoffs with proper efficiency, numbers Luka has. Michael Jordan won two championships with over 37 percent usage in the playoffs, and he did not even really shoot threes in either of those seasons.

Okay, it's time for "basketball theorycrafting that you'll just have to trust me on", since the research on this does not (yet) exist in a way that I can link, though I am working on it. Scroll down in this old post about soccer to find a graph about the so-called "Usage-Efficiency Boundary" which was from the work of Evan Zamir, the original publication of which I cannot find anywhere. Basically, there is a causal relationship between usage rate and efficiency in the NBA that shows that efficiency necessarily decreases as usage increases in basketball; this could be due to fatigue, simple statistical regression from volume or (probably) a mix of both. But Ian Levy, noted basketball nerd, told me once that he found that 3-point efficiency doesn't necessarily follow that same trend, and you might be able to blow through this usage barrier with enough 3-pointers. Hmm…

I'm currently looking into that and how to have a full project on it soon … but what that means is that Luka Doncic could potentially do way better than Harden and Westbrook did with their usage rates if he can keep his 3-point volume up and keep that shooting up, then we could be in business. Stay tuned for updates on this theory.

The only thing Doncic hasn't been this season is the MVP favorite, somehow, since Victor Wembanyama still somehow leads in that department having one of the most destructive two-way seasons I could have possibly imagined. Luka really could become one of the greatest players ever never to win an MVP if this just never breaks for him, which is certainly something to monitor historically, but for this year? I think this Luka could both win his first MVP and win the Lakers a title. I buy this hype, every bit of it, even if it's just because I'm a nerd.

#2647. Despite injury, UND's Tyler Erkman has been steady force in the secondary

Nov. 17—GRAND FORKS — The UND football team's depth at safety has been on shaky ground all season.

For a group already light on experience, veteran Jy Martin was unsuccessful in challenging the NCAA's eligibility rules. To add to the shortage at safety, part-time starter Avery Dixon was injured early in the season and has played in about half of the Fighting Hawks' games in 2026.

That meant the Hawks needed Tyler Erkman to be the steady rock in the defensive back end. The only problem is Erkman has a nagging shoulder injury that constantly required attention throughout fall camp.

In Week 3 at Portland State, the odds of Erkman holding up throughout the year appeared thin when he missed the game because he was re-injured in warm-ups.

But as No. 10 UND searches for an eighth win in the final game of the regular season at 1 p.m. Saturday against Southern Illinois at the Alerus Center, Erkman's surprising durability has been vital for a Fighting Hawks defense playing at its best late in the year.

"I think the coaching staff and training staff put together a great plan," said Erkman, a 6-foot-1, 195-pound senior from Lake Zurich, Ill. "We stuck to it. There were a couple of games where you get banged up but that's football. I knew that coming into the season, but I think we've done a great job managing it."

UND head coach Eric Schmidt said Erkman's durability has been huge.

"It's something we knew early on in the year, really all the way back to spring," Schmidt said. "Just with the timing of things, he was going to have to be able to play through some pain and discomfort."

Erkman is having his best year in Grand Forks in his third season contributing. He had 31 tackles in 2024, 26 in 2025 and has 57 this season, which ranks third on the Hawks' defense only behind starting linebackers Mike Devereaux and Ethan Boll.

"He's been really productive and consistent, but there are certain guys that are like coaches out there, and there are certain positions within our defense that are communicators, and he's done a great job," Schmidt said. "I think guys in front of him can play fast just because of how smart he is, the intelligence he brings, the communication that he brings.

"We have talked a lot around here about winning the pre-snap and the cycle of the snap. He takes that to heart. He understands how important it is for him to be communicating out there so the rest of the guys can go and play with some confidence."

Despite the No. 3-toughest schedule in the FCS, UND leads the Missouri Valley Football Conference and ranks 15th nationally in sacks this season with 28.

"Those guys are so competitive," Erkman said. "It's a race to the quarterback. It makes our job so easy in the secondary. It's great to cover for two seconds when guys like Lance (Rucker) and Braden (Mohr) are going to be back there."

And then there's Kirk Cousins, whose career has swooped and swerved in a way he never can on the field.

Jones would not elaborate with the hosts about the discussions regarding the Cowboys' defense and Parker's standing within the organization.

The two big Super Bowl odds movers this week resulted from one play on Sunday, when Aidan Hutchinson sacked Drake Maye and then Hutchinson proceeded to injure himself on the celebration.

New York Jets head coach Aaron Glenn was hired by the team thanks to his excellence as a defensive coordinator. But after the team struggled on defense during Glenn's first year as head coach, he decided to take over defensive play-calling duties in 2026.

That change lasted just nine games. Glenn told reporters Monday he gave up defensive play-calling ahead of the team's 31-12 loss to the Buffalo Bills in Week 10, per ESPN.

Glenn said the move was made to help the team win games. He added that while Jets defensive coordinator Brian Duker called plays Sunday, Glenn was "very involved" in the team's scheme.

"I've said this and I will continue to do this: Anything I can do as a head coach to help us win games, I'm willing to do it," Glenn said. "I'm not afraid to do that. So I gave him the lead, but I was very involved in what we ran."

#2645. Brewers bash champion Dodgers to brink of NLCS sweep; CBS Sports Preseason All-America team revealed

If not listed, please contact your TV provider.

This is an article version of the CBS Sports HQ AM Newsletter, the ultimate guide to every day in sports. You can sign up to get it in your inbox every weekday morning here.

One of the biggest benefits of the NIL era is that college basketball has more elite talent than ever, now that players are returning for bigger paychecks instead of bolting for NBA money at the first opportunity.

That made selecting our 2026-27 CBS Sports Preseason All-America teams especially difficult, but our experts nailed it. Each of the three teams features players who will be performing at the next level very soon, but the best of those might be Florida superstar Thomas Haugh.

As our own Isaac Trotter explains, if Haugh can improve his range shooting, he won't have to wait long to hear his name called in the 2027 NBA Draft.

When it comes to how the talent broke down by conference, it was a a pretty level playing field for the most part.

Not to spoil anyting, but Arizona freshman Caleb Holt did not make the cut. He did, however, turn some heads in the Wildcats' exhibition game.

Loyalty is an excellent quality to have in a friend or partner. It's also why we love dogs.

It should not be quite as prevalent among college football coaches, some of whom have been undone because they did what was comfortable, not what was necessarily best for the team.

Our own John Talty highlighted five high-profile coaches who have been loyal to a fault, making hires and personnel decisions that have come back to haunt them. One of those coaches is Mike Elko. After a shaky season from Marcel Reed in 2025, Texas A&M chose not to pursue an upgrade in the portal.

Instead, the Aggies gave Reed a major payday, and they'll miss the College Football Playoff because of it.

Look, it can happen to the best of us. Dan Lanning and Dabo Swinney wound up on the list, despite the success that those two have had throughout their careers.

Steve Sarkisian is another coach who has fallen into the trap of being too loyal, but he may have a huge decision on his hands in the offseason. Arch Manning has struggled enough that another year in college should be on the table. If that happens, would Sark welcome back Manning with open arms, despite his shortcomings?

Finally, one person for whom loyalty is no an issue is Missouri QB Austin Simmons. After Trinidad Chambliss won the starting job at Ole Miss last year, Simmons didn't feel the need to stick around, but there won't be bitterness when Simmons returns to Oxford this weekend.

#2644. Can the Raptors avoid 15 losses in a row to the Knicks?

On Sunday, the New York Knicks extended their winning streak over the Toronto Raptors with a dramatic 112-108 overtime win. Scottie Barnes returned to the lineup for Toronto and poured in 30 points but it wasn't enough to stop Toronto's recent slide, as they now sit at 5-8 and 9th in the Eastern Conference. Can the Raptors put an end to their four-game losing streak (and their much longer streak across multiple seasons) against New York?

There's not a lot of new stuff to add since the last preview, since the two teams faced off mere days ago, but there are a few trends worth noting on New York's side. Josh Hart and Mikal Bridges, two-thirds of the Knicks' vaunted "Wingstop" trio have seen their minutes cut as of late, and neither has looked comfortable on the court, particularly on the offensive end. The team's been stuck in some old habits this season, with its starting line digging itself into holes, only for key bench players like Landry Shamet, Deuce McBride, and Jordan Clarkson (suddenly a deadly offensive rebounder and energetic defender well into his thirties) to provide the jolt they need to shake out of their slump.

INDIANAPOLIS, IN – NOVEMBER 13: Jordan Clarkson #00 of the New York Knicks smiles before the game against the Indiana Pacers during the 2026 Emirates NBA Cup on November 13, 2026 at Gainbridge Fieldhouse in Indianapolis, Indiana. NOTE TO USER: User expressly acknowledges and agrees that, by downloading and or using this Photograph, user is consenting to the terms and conditions of the Getty Images License Agreement. Mandatory Copyright Notice: Copyright 2026 NBAE (Photo by Luther Schlaifer/NBAE via Getty Images) | NBAE via Getty Images

It's a troubling sign for the defending champions, one that worked astonishingly well in the playoffs last season, but that has been significantly less successful this year, thanks to some ice-cold shooting from key players. Even Jalen Brunson hasn't been immune to shooting slumps this year, with some of his signature shots inside the arc clanking off the rim more often than usual.

Those same warts reared their ugly heads on Sunday for the Knicks, but, against a Raptors team lacking in firepower and offensive dynamism, it was enough to secure the win, even with Barnes hitting some very difficult jumpers in key moments. Ja'Kobe Walter gave Toronto very little that night, with just seven points on 2-for-8 shooting, Immanuel Quickley's shot dried up after boldly proclaiming "I'm here" following a big bucket, and Collin Murray-Boyles was held to single digits despite snagging four offensive boards.

Even though Brunson led the charge late, Karl-Anthony Towns was the protagonist for New York. He's a major matchup problem for the Raps, too skilled on the perimeter for Jakob Poeltl to deal with comfortably, and considerably bigger than CMB. When the Knicks can space the floor better (i.e. when Hart is on the bench), he can put up buckets in bunches, and he did just that, to the tune of a co-game-high of 28, matching Brunson's total. He can also be a terror on the offensive glass when the Raptors go small, and his five offensive boards were more than even the energetic CMB managed.

The Raptors appeared to have seized control late but the Shamet-Bridges wing duo fared far better than the starting pair, with Shamet's off-ball movement in particular flummoxing a Raptors defence that wasn't always connected for entire possessions late. The former journeyman-turned-semi-starter dropped 23 points on just 12 shots. Meanwhile, they got a few useful minutes from James Wiseman, the former lottery pick-turned-journeyman, in place of Andre Drummond, who, for all of his size and rebounding prowess, seems to be losing his grip on the backup centre spot.

Scottie Barnes put up 30 last game, but it was telling that he had to settle for tough jumpers when matched up against OG Anunoby. Getting Barnes the ball on the move in transition is vital, as is finding ways to get him matched up against smaller players he can bully in halfcourt scenarios. With a lineup a bit light on ballhandling and creativity, the offence goes as Scottie goes and it's vital that they scheme up as many opportunities for him to run free as possible.

Last time around, I said the Knicks are as vulnerable to an upset as they have been in quite some time, and that still stands true. All season, there have been moments where the team has looked like a group of strangers, despite most of them entering their third season together. But, when they turn it on, they can be lethal on both ends. If the Raptors are going to snap their years-long losing streak against them, they'll need to do a much better job taking care of the ball and the defensive glass. Otherwise, they could be in for another disappointing night.

#2643. Vero Beach's Ella Gravlee signs with Florida, where sisterly reunion awaits

VERO BEACH – Due to an unfortunate incident, Ella Gravlee will get to play volleyball with her older sister.

Madi Gravlee received a medical redshirt from the University of Florida in 2025 after tearing her anterior cruciate ligament (ACL). She was able to return this past season for the Gators.

Monday afternoon, Nov. 16 at Vero Beach High's Witt Gymnasium, a signing ceremony was held for Ella and teammate Yahya Johnson (University of Central Florida).

Ella actually made it official Wednesday on National Signing Day, but since there was no school because of Veterans Day, the ceremony was moved to Monday.

More: Vero Beach volleyball stuns Jupiter in wild five-set district final

More: Outside looking in, Vero Beach believes its best volleyball is still ahead

Except for a beach event when both sisters were younger – Madi 16 years old and Ella 12 – the two sisters never played competitively together.

"With her injury and a medical redshirt, we will be able to have a few years together, which is so exciting," Madi said.

Vero Beach High coach Heather Magelssen had the opportunity to do the same with her younger sister Jennifer at Indiana University.

"Isn't that the best thing ever? It is an experience and vibe that will never be broken," Heather Magelssen said. "It's once in a lifetime. And to share those experiences, I'm so happy for her. And I'm so happy for her sister. And I'm so happy for her family."

It will be a complete family affair for the Gravlees. Her mother, then Julie Stanhope (volleyball) and father Russ Gravlee (football) also played for the Gators.

A 6-foot-3 outside hitter Ella first committed to attend Ohio State before switching to Florida.

"I've always been a Gator at heart. I knew that," Ella said. "It's just a token of being there and wanting to compete again. Obviously, nothing bad at Ohio State. They're a fantastic school. I just felt at home when I was at Florida."

And Ella knows who to rely on for inside information concerning Florida Gators volleyball. Madi has been feeding her the inside scoop.

"She just says, especially the last few years, they're such a family," Ella said. "And they're so competitive. And that's what every athlete is looking for: that competitive nature and fighting for your spot. And having such a culture of family, too, it's so important."

And Ella knows how valuable having someone on the inside can make her transition from high school to college.

"Tons," Ella said. "It's such an advantage to have an older sister there to know the ropes and to show you the ropes too. It's unique to have someone to want to show you and want to help you, like (watching) film. It's gonna be a huge jump from high school to college, but it's such a unique experience."

A four-year starter, Ella Gravlee departed Vero Beach High as the career leader in kills with 1,402. An all-around player, she also recorded 1,340 serves received,  783 digs, 159 aces, 82 assists and 79 blocks.

During her senior season, Gravlee notched 350 kills, 176 digs, 43 aces, 20 assists and 15 blocks.

"She's been a great teammate," Johnson said. "She's really competitive. It's really nice to play with somebody who's that competitive."

Magelssen was nearly at a loss for words when asked what Gravlee brought to the Vero Beach High program.

"She elevated our program in a way nobody else could have," Magelssen said. "She set a standard that is elite. She will be missed.

"Ella is an excellent student. She excels in every aspect of her life. It's a hard person to live up to. But she is a great example: the hard work, the determination and the sacrifice she's put in, but it takes a lot. If you want to accomplish those things, these are the things you have to do. It's a process. Ella went through the process. Ella excelled at the process. She's an excellent example for me to use for upcoming athletics.

"I have been blessed to be with her, to learn from her and grow myself."

Gravlee said she can take many of the traits she brought to Vero Beach to Gainesville.

"A big part of my role at Vero was supporting other players," Gravlee said. "Being loud and bringing energy to the court. That's a great thing for me to be able to take to Florida to stay aggressive. At Vero they encouraged me to take aggressive swings and go for things. I can take that with me."

Also a standout beach volleyball player, Gravlee helped Vero Beach reach the FHSAA state semifinals her junior season.

Since she will be heading to Gainesville after the current semester at Vero Beach, Gravlee played her last game on the sand with the Fighting Indians.

"Yes, for sure. I'll definitely miss that this season," Gravlee said.

She also gained valuable experience during her one season with the Winter Park Volleyball Club. Ironically, Vero Beach swept Winter Park, 3-0, in the FHSAA Beach Volleyball Class 3A-Region 2 final last year.

"I played there last year for one season. It's the greatest club season I've ever had," Gravlee said. "I got to work with Isabel Incinelli (Texas A&M commit) Ellie Enger, Alex Kennedy – all these great players. I'm just so grateful for that experience."

Soon Gravlee will add to her many volleyball experiences – playing with her older sister.

An experience that likely will vault to the top of her list.
